science.statement: Infimind translates established findings from cognitive science and educational psychology into a personalised learning system for every student.

principles.name: Retrieval Practice
principles.summary: Students actively recall knowledge instead of relying on repeated rereading.
principles.application: Closed-book recall, cumulative questions, oral explanations and long-term retention checks.

principles.name: Spaced Practice
principles.summary: Learning is revisited over carefully planned intervals.
principles.application: Individual revision calendars, resurfacing of older concepts and memory-health reviews.

principles.name: Successive Relearning
principles.summary: Mastery requires successful recall across multiple separated sessions.
principles.application: Knowledge moves from encountered to understood, retrievable and durable.

principles.name: Interleaved Practice
principles.summary: Related question types are mixed so students learn to select the right method.
principles.application: Mixed practice sets, unfamiliar questions and transfer tasks.

principles.name: Self-Explanation
principles.summary: Students explain why a method works and when it should be applied.
principles.application: Teach-your-mentor activities, explanation journals and reasoning prompts.

principles.name: Elaborative Questioning
principles.summary: Students connect facts to causes, mechanisms and prior knowledge.
principles.application: What, why, how, when and what-changes questioning.

principles.name: Generation
principles.summary: Students attempt, predict and create before receiving complete answers.
principles.application: Supported prediction, partial problems and student-generated examples.

principles.name: Worked Examples and Fading
principles.summary: Support is provided initially and reduced as competence grows.
principles.application: I Do, We Analyse, We Do, You Do, You Explain, You Transfer.

principles.name: Dual Coding
principles.summary: Words and meaningful visuals reveal structure, sequence and relationships.
principles.application: Concept maps, diagrams, process flows, timelines and data representations.

principles.name: Formative Feedback
principles.summary: Assessment guides the next learning step instead of merely producing a score.
principles.application: Error classification, corrective feedback and parallel questions.

principles.name: Metacognitive Calibration
principles.summary: Students compare what they believe they know with what they can actually retrieve.
principles.application: Confidence predictions, post-task reflection and strategy adjustment.

principles.name: Mastery-Oriented Goals
principles.summary: Academic ambitions are translated into specific, controllable learning behaviours.
principles.application: Outcome goals, learning goals and measurable process commitments.

science.disclaimer: Infimind does not claim that one technique works identically for every student. We use evidence to select, combine and adapt learning strategies according to the learner, subject, goal and context.
